text.p: CS First Boston (CSFB) said on Thursday it maintained its "buy" recommendation on the shares of Hungarian plastics industrial company Pannonplast following the release of its preliminary 1996 consolidated IAS results.

"The gross margin for the full year was 35.2 percent, below our forecast of 36.1 percent and net income was also slightly below our expectations, but our basic outlook for the stock remains positive," CSFB's analyst Spencer Jakab said in a company update.
"Even in this frothy market Pannonplast remains good value."
Pannonplast reported a net income of 1.42 billion forints for 1996 on sales of 9.67 billion against a net profit of 838.2 million forints on sales of 8.28 billion in 1995.

"With relatively lower sales revenues due to depressed raw material prices as well as improving gross and net margins, the group generated a net income of 1.42 billion forints," Pannonplast said in its earnings report.
Pannonplast's sales revenues rose by 16.9 percent year-on-year. Relatively depressed international raw material prices were the main reason for below-inflation growth, the company said.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange Pannonplast shares closed at 7,100 forints, up 150.
